messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Exposing (non-normalized) Incomplete Beta Function
parts:
> What's unstable? Is it some kind of range thing where
> we can just fail if they're outside that range?
> Or is the usual numerical instability of auto-diffing
> an iterative algorithm?

Both. The functions themselves are poorly implemented power
series and derivatives would be even worse (wether the series
were diff’d by hand or the autodiff was used explicity).

> And if so, do you know how to do it
> better? Presumably you (Michael) have some solution up your sleeve
> for the new autodiff at higher orders.

Don’t allow CDFs for higher-order methods? The new autodiff
has exections for functions without higher-order partials implemented
for exactly this purpose.

The real problem is that stable numerical implementations of these
nasty functions is way beyond our expertise. If I had a few months
I might be able to find the old references, learn all the tricks, and
then implement them for everything. But I don’t.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Exposing (non-normalized) Incomplete Beta Function
parts:
I'm OK with not allowing higher-order autodiffs.

We can throw exceptions, which will get the user the point
eventually.

It'd also be helpful if we listed functions with higher-order
autodiff in the manual. Even better if we could warn users
at compile time. I'd like it even better if we could throw
errors at compile time, but it's not clear we're going to know
what they're going to call when they compile.

- Bob
